title: Annealed Canary Controller with SLO-aware Safety Windows
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Current progressive delivery tooling at Redwood uses fixed percentage ramps and static gate thresholds for canaries. That approach requires a lot of manual tuning per release and often leads to either overly conservative ramps that slow rollouts or overly aggressive ramps that trigger noisy rollbacks. We need an automated controller that can 'anneal' traffic ramps based on live SLO telemetry, safety windows, and historical release variance so releases can complete faster while respecting production safety constraints.
background: Recent incidents during runtime-1.18 and runtime-1.19 rollouts showed that fixed ramps failed to account for varying tail-latency characteristics in different model families and customer cohorts. On two occasions on-call had to abort rollouts because the static 20%->50% step breached p99 latency SLOs for a subset of LTS customers. Engineering and SRE requested a system that adapts ramp velocity to observed SLO headroom and maintains a safety window to avoid oscillation.
proposal_summary: Implement an 'Annealed Canary Controller' (ACC): a rollout controller that schedules percentage ramps using an annealing function (initial cautious steps, gradually increasing step sizes as confidence improves) and couples ramp decisions to SLO-derived health signals and a safety window cooldown. Key features: SLO-aware ramp gating, adaptive step-sizing, hold-and-retry logic, automatic rollback predicates, and audit events for Console visibility. The controller will expose tunables via rollout policies and integrate with existing rollout API and telemetry exporters.
design_notes:
- Annealing schedule uses a configurable base schedule and an adaptive multiplier derived from a confidence score (0..1). Confidence is computed from recent metric variance, anomaly detectors, and successful shadow traffic runs.
- Safety window: after any step, the controller enforces a minimum observation period (default 5m) before progressing; if metrics degrade beyond thresholds the controller will either step back or initiate rollback.
- SLO inputs: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and model-quality regressions (if available from evaluations). Each input maps to weighted health penalty.
- Rollout policy schema additions: 'anneal.enabled', 'anneal.base_schedule', 'anneal.max_step', 'slo_thresholds', 'cooldown_secs', 'rollback_policy'.
- Integration points: routing layer for traffic shifts, telemetry ingestion (Console metrics DSL), and rollout audit events in the Console activity feed.
- Safety nets: shadow verification runs, pre-step synthetic probes, and manual hold capability.
acceptance_criteria: Controller implements annealing schedule and exposes policy fields in rollout API
Controller evaluates SLO signals and makes deterministic decisions under unit tests
E2E simulation harness shows faster median time-to-100% compared to static ramps without increasing rollback rate by >5%
Console shows per-step audit events with reason codes and metric snapshots
Automatic rollback triggers when composite health score crosses configured threshold
Documentation and runbook updated; on-call notified and trained on new behavior
implementation_steps: Design API for rollout policy extensions and review with PM and Console owners
Prototype controller logic in feature branch with simulation harness (use synthetic traffic traces)
Add telemetry adapters to compute composite confidence and health scores
Wire controller decisions to routing API and implement audit event emission
Implement rollback and step-back strategies, add unit and integration tests
Run staged experiments on lower-risk namespaces, collect metrics, iterate
Ship behind feature flag and enable for selected internal teams before customer rollout
monitoring_and_metrics: time_to_100pct: time from rollout start to full traffic
rollback_rate: fraction of rollouts that triggered auto-rollback
step_failure_rate: fraction of steps that caused a hold or rollback
post_rollout_regressions: delta in p99 latency and error rate after rollout
confidence_score_distribution: histogram of computed confidence during rollouts
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting anneal rules to internal traces. Mitigation: validate on diverse historical rollouts and include conservative defaults.
Risk: Alert fatigue from more fine-grained audit events. Mitigation: aggregate and surface only actionable alerts; allow Console filters.
Risk: Incorrect SLO weighting causing false rollbacks. Mitigation: staged enablement, and require manual approval for auto-rollback for LTS channels initially.
Risk: Performance impact of controller decisions. Mitigation: compute decisions in a lightweight streaming service with caching and rate limits.
open_questions: Should auto-rollback be disabled by default for LTS customers?
What is the canonical confidence computation and who owns its tuning?
How should model-quality signals from evaluation pipelines be normalized vs latency signals?
What are the UI controls Console needs to present (manual hold, override, step history)?
